newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bank of France leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bank of France leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The French central bank left key interest rates unchanged after a meeting of its monetary policy council on Thursday, in line with the predictions of economists.
The policy meeting came just two days after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided to hike rates for the first time in two years.

A majority of economists polled by Reuters on Wednesday said they did not see the Bank of France cutting the key intervention rate this week, nor or in the coming weeks, but that they still believed rates could come down slightly further in France.

The intervention rate was left unchanged at 3.10 percent and the Bank also left the other official rate, the five-to-10 day rate, untouched at 4.60 percent. The intervention rate was last cut, from 3.15 percent, on January 30, 1997.
There are dissident voices who say the French rate cut cycle may be over and another U.S. rate increase cannot be ruled out after Tuesday's hike to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent.

But most economists believe the French central bank can use its margin over Germany -- the French intervention rate is just a tenth of a percent higher than Germany's key repo rate of 3.0 percent -- to whittle rates further without jeopardising its policy of a maintaining strong franc linked to the German mark.
Because of the Easter holiday on Monday, the next rate-setting money market tender in France takes place a day later, on Tuesday.
